newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico taps new Chiapas peace negotiator.
newsitem.headline: Mexico taps new Chiapas peace negotiator.

text.p: Mexico on Sunday named a veteran politician as peace negotiator with Zapatista Indian rebels in southern Chiapas state, officials said.

Pedro Joaquin Coldwell, a former minister of tourism in the early 1990s, was tapped by President Ernesto Zedillo to head the government delegation to the talks, which broke down earlier this year on issues of Indian autonomy.
Coldwell, 47, replaces Marco Antonio Bernal, a ruling party politician who is running for a senate seat in upcoming mid-term elections in July.
Coldwell was also a former governor of Quintana Roo state in the 1980s and secretary general of the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party, according to state-owned news agency Notimex.

The Zapatista guerrillas took up arms in January, 1994 to demand greater democracy and rights for the region's impoverished Indians. At least 150 people died in two weeks of fighting, but a ceasefire has since held while both sides have tried to reach a final peace accord.

The Zapatistas' charismatic leader, Subcommander Marcos, broke off talks in January when the government tried to revise an agreement on Indian rights reached between the rebels and a legislative government commission.
Zedillo also named Alejandro Carrillo Castro, 56, as the government's chief spokesman. Carrillo worked in the finance ministry in the 1970s, Notimex said.
